sanskrit: tatas tyajati so 'vyaktaṃ sargapralayadharmiṇam nirguṇaḥ prakṛtiṃ veda guṇayuktām acetanām
english: Then he forsakes the Unmanifest, whose nature is creation and dissolution; free of the qualities, he knows Nature to be bound up with the qualities and devoid of consciousness.

sanskrit: tataḥ kevaladharmāsau bhavaty avyaktadarśanāt kevalena samāgamya vimukto ''tmānam āpnuyāt
english: Thereupon, through his vision of the Unmanifest, he becomes one whose nature is absolute; uniting with the Absolute and liberated, he attains the Self.

sanskrit: etat tat tattvam ity āhur nistattvam ajarāmaram tattvasaṃśrayaṇād etat tattvavan na ca mānada pañcaviṃśatitattvāni pravadanti manīṣiṇaḥ
english: This, they say, is that Reality, itself beyond the principles, ageless and deathless; through its dependence on the principles it seems to possess them, yet it does not, O bestower of honor. The wise declare that the principles are twenty-five.

sanskrit: na caiṣa tattvavāṃs tāta nistattvas tv eṣa buddhimān eṣa muñcati tattvaṃ hi kṣipraṃ buddhasya lakṣaṇam
english: This one, my son, does not possess the principles; rather, the wise one is beyond the principles. He swiftly relinquishes the principles, for that is the mark of the awakened.

sanskrit: ṣaḍviṃśo 'ham iti prājño gṛhyamāṇo 'jarāmaraḥ kevalena balenaiva samatāṃ yāty asaṃśayam
english: "I am the twenty-sixth"—when the wise man is grasped by this knowledge, ageless and deathless, by the power of the Absolute alone he attains identity with it, beyond all doubt.

sanskrit: ṣaḍviṃśena prabuddhena budhyamāno 'py abuddhimān etan nānātvam ity uktaṃ sāṃkhyaśrutinidarśanāt
english: Awakened by the twenty-sixth yet still in the act of awakening, he is not yet fully wise: this is what is called their difference, taught from the testimony of the Sāṃkhya scriptures.

sanskrit: cetanena sametasya pañcaviṃśatikasya ca ekatvaṃ vai bhavaty asya yadā buddhyā na budhyate
english: For the twenty-fifth principle, joined with the conscious one, there arises oneness with it, so long as it does not awaken through the intellect to the distinction.

sanskrit: budhyamāno 'prabuddhena samatāṃ yāti maithila saṅgadharmā bhavaty eṣa niḥsaṅgātmā narādhipa
english: Awakening, it attains identity with the unawakened, O Maithila; this Self, free of attachment by nature, thus comes to bear the character of attachment, O lord of men.

sanskrit: niḥsaṅgātmānam āsādya ṣaḍviṃśakam ajaṃ viduḥ vibhus tyajati cāvyaktaṃ yadā tv etad vibudhyate caturviṃśam agādhaṃ ca ṣaḍviṃśasya prabodhanāt
english: But on reaching the Self that is free of attachment, they know the twenty-sixth, the unborn; the all-pervading one forsakes the Unmanifest when it awakens to this, and through the awakening of the twenty-sixth it forsakes also the unfathomable twenty-fourth.

sanskrit: eṣa hy apratibuddhaś ca budhyamānaś ca te 'nagha prokto buddhaś ca tattvena yathāśrutinidarśanāt nānātvaikatvam etāvad draṣṭavyaṃ śāstradṛṣṭibhiḥ
english: This, O sinless one, has been explained to you as the unawakened, the awakening, and the truly awakened, according to the testimony of scripture; just so much of their difference and oneness is to be discerned by those whose sight is the teaching.

sanskrit: maśakodumbare yadvad anyatvaṃ tadvad etayoḥ matsyo 'mbhasi yathā tadvad anyatvam upalabhyate
english: As the gnat is other than the fig in which it dwells, so are these two distinct; as a fish in water is other than the water, so is their difference perceived.

sanskrit: evam evāvagantavyaṃ nānātvaikatvam etayoḥ etad vimokṣa ity uktam avyaktajñānasaṃhitam
english: Just so is the difference and the oneness of these two to be understood; this, bound up with the knowledge of the Unmanifest, is declared to be liberation.

sanskrit: pañcaviṃśatikasyāsya yo 'yaṃ deheṣu vartate eṣa mokṣayitavyeti prāhur avyaktagocarāt
english: This twenty-fifth principle, which abides within bodies, is the one that must be set free—so they declare—out from the domain of the Unmanifest.

sanskrit: so 'yam evaṃ vimucyeta nānyatheti viniścayaḥ pareṇa paradharmā ca bhavaty eṣa sametya vai
english: Thus and not otherwise is it freed: such is the settled conclusion. Uniting with the Supreme, it takes on the nature of the Supreme.

sanskrit: viśuddhadharmā śuddhena buddhena ca sa buddhimān vimuktadharmā muktena sametya puruṣarṣabha
english: Uniting with the pure, it becomes pure in nature; with the awakened, it becomes wise; with the liberated, its nature becomes that of the liberated, O bull among men.

sanskrit: niyogadharmiṇā caiva niyogātmā bhavaty api vimokṣiṇā vimokṣaś ca sametyeha tathā bhavet
english: Uniting with one bound to duty, it takes on the character of duty; and uniting with the liberator, it likewise becomes liberation itself here.

sanskrit: śucikarmā śuciś caiva bhavaty amitadīptimān vimalātmā ca bhavati sametya vimalātmanā
english: Of pure deeds and pure it becomes, of measureless radiance; and uniting with the stainless Self, it too becomes stainless of soul.

sanskrit: kevalātmā tathā caiva kevalena sametya vai svatantraś ca svatantreṇa svatantratvam avāpnute
english: So too, uniting with the Absolute, it becomes absolute in soul; and uniting with the independent, it attains independence.

sanskrit: etāvad etat kathitaṃ mayā te; tathyaṃ mahārāja yathārthatattvam amatsaratvaṃ pratigṛhya cārthaṃ; sanātanaṃ brahma viśuddham ādyam
english: This much have I told you truly, O great king, in its real and very essence; receive this teaching without envy—the eternal Brahman, pure and primordial.

sanskrit: na vedaniṣṭhasya janasya rājan; pradeyam etat paramaṃ tvayā bhavet vivitsamānāya vibodhakārakaṃ; prabodhahetoḥ praṇatasya śāsanam
english: To a man merely devoted to the letter of the Veda, O king, this supreme teaching should not be given by you; but to one who longs to know, this enlightening instruction—for the sake of awakening—should be given to him who bows in reverence.

sanskrit: na deyam etac ca tathānṛtātmane; śaṭhāya klībāya na jihmabuddhaye na paṇḍitajñānaparopatāpine; deyaṃ tvayedaṃ vinibodha yādṛśe
english: Nor is it to be given to the man of false soul, to the deceitful, to the coward, to the crooked of mind, nor to one who flaunts learning to torment others; learn now to whom you should give it.

sanskrit: śraddhānvitāyātha guṇānvitāya; parāpavādād viratāya nityam viśuddhayogāya budhāya caiva; kriyāvate 'tha kṣamiṇe hitāya
english: To one endowed with faith and with virtues, ever turned away from slandering others, to one of pure discipline and wise, active in rites, forbearing, and benevolent.

sanskrit: viviktaśīlāya vidhipriyāya; vivādahīnāya bahuśrutāya vijānate caiva na cāhitakṣame; dame ca śaktāya śame ca dehinām
english: To one of solitary conduct who loves the sacred rule, free of contention, deeply learned and discerning, who does not condone what is harmful, and is capable of restraint and of the inner peace of embodied beings.

sanskrit: etair guṇair hīnatame na deyam; etat paraṃ brahma viśuddham āhuḥ na śreyasā yokṣyati tādṛśe kṛtaṃ; dharmapravaktāram apātradānāt
english: To one most destitute of these virtues it must not be given—this supreme Brahman, which they call utterly pure; what is bestowed on such a one will not be joined with blessing, and by giving to the unworthy the teacher of dharma himself loses his merit.

sanskrit: pṛthvīm imāṃ yady api ratnapūrṇāṃ; dadyān nadeyaṃ tv idam avratāya jitendriyāyaitad asaṃśayaṃ te; bhavet pradeyaṃ paramaṃ narendra
english: Even though one offered this whole earth filled with jewels, this is not to be given to a man without vows; but to one who has mastered his senses, this supreme teaching should without doubt be imparted by you, O lord of men.

sanskrit: karāla mā te bhayam astu kiṃ cid; etac chrutaṃ brahma paraṃ tvayādya yathāvad uktaṃ paramaṃ pavitraṃ; niḥśokam atyantam anādimadhyam
english: Karāla, let no fear of any kind be yours; today you have heard this supreme Brahman, declared just as it is—most sacred, sorrowless, utterly without beginning or middle.

sanskrit: agādhajanmāmaraṇaṃ ca rājan; nirāmayaṃ vītabhayaṃ śivaṃ ca samīkṣya mohaṃ tyaja cādya sarvaṃ; jñānasya tattvārtham idaṃ viditvā
english: Unfathomable in birth, deathless, O king, free of disease, fear gone, and auspicious—looking upon it, cast off now all delusion, having understood this, the very essence of knowledge.

sanskrit: avāptam etad dhi purā sanātanād; dhiraṇyagarbhād gadato narādhipa prasādya yatnena tam ugratejasaṃ; sanātanaṃ brahma yathādya vai tvayā
english: This was obtained of old from the eternal Hiraṇyagarbha as he spoke it, O lord of men, when by earnest effort that one of fierce splendor had been won over—just as the eternal Brahman has now been won by you.

sanskrit: pṛṣṭas tvayā cāsmi yathā narendra; tathā mayedaṃ tvayi coktam adya tathāvāptaṃ brahmaṇo me narendra; mahaj jñānaṃ mokṣavidāṃ purāṇam
english: As you have questioned me, O lord of men, so have I declared this to you today; thus did I obtain from Brahman that great and ancient knowledge of those who know liberation, O lord of men.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca etad uktaṃ paraṃ brahma yasmān nāvartate punaḥ pañcaviṃśo mahārāja paramarṣinidarśanāt
english: Bhīṣma said: This has been declared the supreme Brahman, from which the twenty-fifth returns no more, O great king, according to the testimony of the highest seers.

sanskrit: punarāvṛttim āpnoti paraṃ jñānam avāpya ca nāvabudhyati tattvena budhyamāno 'jarāmaraḥ
english: He who, even after attaining supreme knowledge, does not truly awaken, though awakening, undergoes return again; but the one who knows it as it is becomes ageless and deathless.

sanskrit: etan niḥśreyasakaraṃ jñānānāṃ te paraṃ mayā kathitaṃ tattvatas tāta śrutvā devarṣito nṛpa
english: This highest of all knowledges, which brings the supreme good, I have told you truly, my son, having myself heard it from the divine seer, O king.

sanskrit: hiraṇyagarbhād ṛṣiṇā vasiṣṭhena mahātmanā vasiṣṭhād ṛṣiśārdūlān nārado 'vāptavān idam
english: From Hiraṇyagarbha the great-souled seer Vasiṣṭha received it, and from Vasiṣṭha, tiger among seers, Nārada obtained this.

sanskrit: nāradād viditaṃ mahyam etad brahma sanātanam mā śucaḥ kauravendra tvaṃ śrutvaitat paramaṃ padam
english: From Nārada this eternal Brahman became known to me. Grieve not, O lord of the Kurus, now that you have heard this supreme state.

sanskrit: yena kṣarākṣare vitte na bhayaṃ tasya vidyate vidyate tu bhayaṃ tasya yo naitad vetti pārthiva
english: For him by whom the perishable and the imperishable are known, no fear exists; but fear does exist for him who does not know this, O son of Pṛthā.

sanskrit: avijñānāc ca mūḍhātmā punaḥ punar upadravan pretya jātisahasrāṇi maraṇāntāny upāśnute
english: And the deluded soul, through ignorance, suffering torment again and again, undergoes after death thousands of births, each ending in death.

sanskrit: devalokaṃ tathā tiryaṅ mānuṣyam api cāśnute yadi śudhyati kālena tasmād ajñānasāgarāt
english: He passes through the world of the gods, the animal realm, and the human state as well, if in time he is purified out of that ocean of ignorance.

sanskrit: ajñānasāgaro ghoro hy avyakto 'gādha ucyate ahany ahani majjanti yatra bhūtāni bhārata
english: The dreadful ocean of ignorance is called the Unmanifest, the unfathomable, wherein day after day living beings are submerged, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: yasmād agādhād avyaktād uttīrṇas tvaṃ sanātanāt tasmāt tvaṃ virajāś caiva vitamaskaś ca pārthiva
english: Since you have crossed beyond that unfathomable, eternal Unmanifest, therefore you are free of passion and free of darkness, O son of Pṛthā.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca mṛgayāṃ vicaran kaś cid vijane janakātmajaḥ vane dadarśa viprendram ṛṣiṃ vaṃśadharaṃ bhṛgoḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: A certain son of Janaka, while roaming in the hunt through a lonely place, beheld in the forest a lord of brahmins, a seer who carried on the lineage of Bhṛgu.

sanskrit: tam āsīnam upāsīnaḥ praṇamya śirasā munim paścād anumatas tena papraccha vasumān idam
english: Seating himself near that seated sage and bowing his head in reverence, then with the seer's leave, the prince Vasumat asked him this.

sanskrit: bhagavan kim idaṃ śreyaḥ pretya vāpīha vā bhavet puruṣasyādhruve dehe kāmasya vaśavartinaḥ
english: "Holy one, what is that good which avails a man, here or hereafter, when his body is impermanent and he is in the grip of desire?"

sanskrit: satkṛtya paripṛṣṭaḥ san sumahātmā mahātapāḥ nijagāda tatas tasmai śreyaskaram idaṃ vacaḥ
english: Thus honored and questioned, the great-souled one of mighty austerity then spoke to him this word that brings about the good.

sanskrit: manaso 'pratikūlāni pretya ceha ca vāñchasi bhūtānāṃ pratikūlebhyo nivartasva yatendriyaḥ
english: "If you desire what is not contrary to the mind, here and hereafter, then with senses restrained turn away from whatever is hurtful to living beings.

sanskrit: dharmaḥ satāṃ hitaḥ puṃsāṃ dharmaś caivāśrayaḥ satām dharmāl lokās trayas tāta pravṛttāḥ sacarācarāḥ
english: Dharma is the welfare of good men; dharma is the refuge of the good. From dharma, my son, the three worlds with all that moves and is unmoving have come forth.

sanskrit: svādukāmuka kāmānāṃ vaitṛṣṇyaṃ kiṃ na gacchasi madhu paśyasi durbuddhe prapātaṃ nānupaśyasi
english: O craver of sweet things, why do you not reach freedom from thirst for desires? You see the honey, dull-witted one, but you do not see the precipice beneath.

sanskrit: yathā jñāne paricayaḥ kartavyas tatphalārthinā tathā dharme paricayaḥ kartavyas tatphalārthinā
english: Just as familiarity with knowledge must be cultivated by one who seeks its fruit, so too familiarity with dharma must be cultivated by one who seeks its fruit.

sanskrit: asatā dharmakāmena viśuddhaṃ karma duṣkaram satā tu dharmakāmena sukaraṃ karma duṣkaram
english: For a bad man who desires dharma, pure action is hard to accomplish; but for a good man who desires dharma, even hard action is easily done.

sanskrit: vane grāmyasukhācāro yathā grāmyas tathaiva saḥ grāme vanasukhācāro yathā vanacaras tathā
english: He who in the forest pursues the pleasures of the village is no better than a villager; while he who in the village lives by the conduct of the forest is as one who dwells in the wild.

sanskrit: manovākkarmake dharme kuru śraddhāṃ samāhitaḥ nivṛttau vā pravṛttau vā saṃpradhārya guṇāguṇān
english: In the dharma of thought, word, and deed place your faith with a collected mind, having weighed the merits and demerits of withdrawal or of action.

sanskrit: nityaṃ ca bahu dātavyaṃ sādhubhyaś cānasūyatā prārthitaṃ vrataśaucābhyāṃ satkṛtaṃ deśakālayoḥ
english: And one should ever give abundantly to good men, free of envy, what has been sought with vows and purity and offered with honor at the proper place and time.

sanskrit: śubhena vidhinā labdham arhāya pratipādayet krodham utsṛjya dattvā ca nānutapyen na kīrtayet
english: What has been gained by righteous means one should bestow upon the worthy, casting off anger; and having given, one should neither regret it nor boast of it.

sanskrit: anṛśaṃsaḥ śucir dāntaḥ satyavāg ārjave sthitaḥ yonikarmaviśuddhaś ca pātraṃ syād vedavid dvijaḥ
english: Free of cruelty, pure, self-controlled, truthful of speech, established in uprightness, pure in birth and conduct, and learned in the Veda—such a brahmin is a worthy recipient.

sanskrit: satkṛtā caikapatnī ca jātyā yonir iheṣyate ṛgyajuḥsāmago vidvān ṣaṭkarmā pātram ucyate
english: A wife honored and devoted to one husband is desired here for the purity of lineage in birth; and the learned one who chants Ṛk, Yajus, and Sāman and performs the six rites is called a worthy recipient.

sanskrit: sa eva dharmaḥ so 'dharmas taṃ taṃ pratinaraṃ bhavet pātrakarmaviśeṣeṇa deśakālāv avekṣya ca
english: The very same act may be dharma or adharma with respect to each particular man, according to the distinction of recipient and deed, and with regard to place and time.

sanskrit: līlayālpaṃ yathā gātrāt pramṛjyād rajasaḥ pumān bahuyatnena mahatā pāpanirharaṇaṃ tathā
english: As a man wipes a little dust from his limb with ease, so the removal of sin is accomplished only by great and strenuous effort.

sanskrit: viriktasya yathā samyag ghṛtaṃ bhavati bheṣajam tathā nirhṛtadoṣasya pretyadharmaḥ sukhāvahaḥ
english: As clarified butter becomes a wholesome medicine for one who has been duly purged, so the dharma that bears on the hereafter brings happiness to one whose faults have been expelled.

sanskrit: mānasaṃ sarvabhūteṣu vartate vai śubhāśubhe aśubhebhyaḥ samākṣipya śubheṣv evāvatārayet
english: The mind moves among all beings, toward the good and toward the evil; drawing it away from the evil, one should set it down upon the good alone.

sanskrit: sarvaṃ sarveṇa sarvatra kriyamāṇaṃ ca pūjaya svadharme yatra rāgas te kāmaṃ dharmo vidhīyatām
english: Honor all that is done, by all, everywhere; and wherever your inclination lies within your own dharma, there let dharma be ordained at your pleasure.

sanskrit: adhṛtātman dhṛtau tiṣṭha durbuddhe buddhimān bhava apraśānta praśāmya tvam aprājña prājñavac cara
english: O man of unsteady soul, stand firm in resolve; dull-witted one, become wise; O unquiet one, grow calm; O foolish one, conduct yourself as the wise do.

sanskrit: tejasā śakyate prāptum upāyasahacāriṇā iha ca pretya ca śreyas tasya mūlaṃ dhṛtiḥ parā
english: The good, here and hereafter, can be attained by inner energy accompanied by right means; and the root of that is supreme steadfastness.

sanskrit: rājarṣir adhṛtiḥ svargāt patito hi mahābhiṣaḥ yayātiḥ kṣīṇapuṇyaś ca dhṛtyā lokān avāptavān
english: The royal seer Mahābhiṣa, lacking steadfastness, fell from heaven; while Yayāti, his merit spent, regained the worlds through steadfastness.

sanskrit: tapasvināṃ dharmavatāṃ viduṣāṃ copasevanāt prāpsyase vipulāṃ buddhiṃ tathā śreyo 'bhipatsyase
english: By attending upon ascetics, the righteous, and the learned, you will gain abundant understanding, and so will you come to the good."

sanskrit: sa tu svabhāvasaṃpannas tac chrutvā munibhāṣitam vinivartya manaḥ kāmād dharme buddhiṃ cakāra ha
english: And he, endowed with a noble nature, having heard the words spoken by the sage, turned his mind away from desire and set his understanding upon dharma.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca dharmādharmavimuktaṃ yad vimuktaṃ sarvasaṃśrayāt janmamṛtyuvimuktaṃ ca vimuktaṃ puṇyapāpayoḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: That which is freed from dharma and adharma, freed from all dependence, freed from birth and death, and freed from merit and demerit—

sanskrit: yac chivaṃ nityam abhayaṃ nityaṃ cākṣaram avyayam śuci nityam anāyāsaṃ tad bhavān vaktum arhati
english: that which is auspicious, eternal, fearless, ever imperishable and undecaying, pure, eternal, and effortless—of that you ought to speak.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atra te vartayiṣye 'ham itihāsaṃ purātanam yājñavalkyasya saṃvādaṃ janakasya ca bhārata
english: Bhīṣma said: On this I shall relate to you an ancient tale, the dialogue of Yājñavalkya with Janaka, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: yājñavalkyam ṛṣiśreṣṭhaṃ daivarātir mahāyaśāḥ papraccha janako rājā praśnaṃ praśnavidāṃ varaḥ
english: The illustrious Janaka, son of Daivarāti, foremost among those skilled in questioning, put a question to Yājñavalkya, the best of seers.

sanskrit: katīndriyāṇi viprarṣe kati prakṛtayaḥ smṛtāḥ kim avyaktaṃ paraṃ brahma tasmāc ca paratas tu kim
english: "How many are the senses, O brahmin-seer? How many are the primary natures held to be? What is the Unmanifest, what the supreme Brahman, and what lies beyond even that?

sanskrit: prabhavaṃ cāpyayaṃ caiva kālasaṃkhyāṃ tathaiva ca vaktum arhasi viprendra tvadanugrahakāṅkṣiṇaḥ
english: Of the origin and the dissolution, and likewise of the reckoning of time, you ought to speak, O lord of brahmins, to me who longs for your grace.

sanskrit: ajñānāt paripṛcchāmi tvaṃ hi jñānamayo nidhiḥ tad ahaṃ śrotum icchāmi sarvam etad asaṃśayam
english: Out of ignorance I question you, for you are a treasury made wholly of knowledge; I wish to hear all of this beyond any doubt."

sanskrit: yājñavalkya uvāca śrūyatām avanīpāla yad etad anupṛcchasi yogānāṃ paramaṃ jñānaṃ sāṃkhyānāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ
english: Yājñavalkya said: Hear, O guardian of the earth, what you ask after—the supreme knowledge of the followers of Yoga, and of the followers of Sāṃkhya especially.

sanskrit: na tavāviditaṃ kiṃ cin māṃ tu jijñāsate bhavān pṛṣṭena cāpi vaktavyam eṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ
english: There is nothing unknown to you; yet you wish to test me. Still, when questioned one must answer—this is the eternal law.

sanskrit: aṣṭau prakṛtayaḥ proktā vikārāś cāpi ṣoḍaśa atha sapta tu vyaktāni prāhur adhyātmacintakāḥ
english: Eight are the primary natures declared, and sixteen the modifications; and the contemplators of the inner self say there are seven that are manifest.

sanskrit: avyaktaṃ ca mahāṃś caiva tathāhaṃkāra eva ca pṛthivī vāyur ākāśam āpo jyotiś ca pañcamam
english: The Unmanifest, the Great One, and the I-maker; earth, wind, ether, water, and fire as the fifth—

sanskrit: etāḥ prakṛtayas tv aṣṭau vikārān api me śṛṇu śrotraṃ tvak caiva cakṣuś ca jihvā ghrāṇaṃ ca pañcamam
english: these are the eight primary natures; now hear from me also the modifications: hearing, skin, eye, tongue, and smell as the fifth—

sanskrit: śabdasparśau ca rūpaṃ ca raso gandhas tathaiva ca vāk ca hastau ca pādau ca pāyur meḍhraṃ tathaiva ca
english: sound and touch, form, taste, and likewise smell; speech, the two hands, the two feet, the organ of excretion, and the organ of generation as well—

sanskrit: ete viśeṣā rājendra mahābhūteṣu pañcasu buddhīndriyāṇy athaitāni saviśeṣāṇi maithila
english: these are the particulars within the five great elements, O lord of kings; and these, the organs of cognition together with their particulars, O Maithila—

sanskrit: manaḥ ṣoḍaśakaṃ prāhur adhyātmagaticintakāḥ tvaṃ caivānye ca vidvāṃsas tattvabuddhiviśāradāḥ
english: the mind they declare to be the sixteenth—they who contemplate the course of the inner self, both you and other learned men skilled in the discernment of the principles.

sanskrit: avyaktāc ca mahān ātmā samutpadyati pārthiva prathamaṃ sargam ity etad āhuḥ prādhānikaṃ budhāḥ
english: From the Unmanifest the Great Self arises, O son of Pṛthā; this the wise call the first creation, born of the primordial Nature.
